title: Redesign sparkline hit-testing + streaming tooltip to reduce DOM churn and improve a11y
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: High-density time-series sparkline components are causing excessive DOM nodes during hover interactions (per-point markers + per-tooltip DOM) and slow keyboard navigation for screen-reader users. Mobile and low-power devices see janky hover/drag interactions when many series are overlaid. We also have inconsistent spacing/interaction tokens across chart components leading to duplicated CSS and extra reflows.

Goal: Rework hit-testing and tooltip delivery for sparklines/time-series so that we: 1) maintain precise hover/keyboard accessibility, 2) avoid creating per-point DOM elements, 3) stream tooltip content progressively (first context summary, then per-series details) and 4) consolidate interaction tokens so spacing and hit target are consistent across charts and buttons embedded in legends.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hover/hover-drag over a high-density chart with 10k sampled points does not create more than 12 additional DOM nodes for the tooltip overlay (measured using Lighthouse DOM nodes metric).
2) Time-to-first-tooltip-content <= 40ms on a simulated mid-tier laptop (Core i5, 8GB) and <= 90ms on a mid-tier mobile emulation.
3) Keyboard focus moves between series/legend entries with an announced summary via aria-live before exposing per-series numbers.
4) No regressions in existing unit tests for charts; +1 integration test that validates progressive streaming of tooltip payload.
5) Tokens consolidated: chart.interaction.padding, chart.interaction.hotRadius, chart.tooltip.transitionDuration are added to design tokens and used by chart library and CSS components.
6) PR includes a perf dashboard spike (link) showing 50% reduction in tooltip-related JS heap allocations and 60% fewer layout recalculations on sample workload.
design_notes:
Proposed approach:
- Replace per-point DOM hit targets with a single SVG overlay that computes nearest-neighbor hit via spatial index (striped KD-tree / grid buckets) in the renderer thread.
- Keep a single DOM tooltip container; populate it progressively. Show minimal header (time + aggregate delta) synchronously, then stream series rows as they are resolved from renderer. This reduces initial render work and aids perceived latency.
- Introduce chart.interaction.hotRadius token (defaults: 8px desktop, 12px touch) to control hit acceptance; use CSS vars to keep layout minimal.
- Keyboard accessibility: implement a lightweight focus manager that maps virtual focus slots to series/legend items. On focus, announce a brief summary via aria-live="polite" then update with details after 150ms. Provide an opt-in setting for verbose mode.
- For very high-density series, perform progressive decimation for display-only mode and enable precise point inspection only when user explicitly holds a modifier key (option/alt) — documented as part of UX affordance.
- Add unit test harness for spatial index correctness and perf regression benchmark under CI (sample dataset attached).
tradeoffs:
- Offloading hit-testing to a spatial index increases JS memory for index structures but reduces DOM churn and paint time.
- Progressive streaming improves perceived latency but complicates tooltip animation states; we will standardize a three-stage state machine (placeholder -> header -> details) to keep animations consistent.
- Modifier-key for exact inspection reduces immediacy of precise point selection; mitigated by clear affordance and keyboard alternative (focus+enter).

Engineering: implement spatial index-based hit testing in canvas/svg renderer (ENG- expected subtask to be created)
Engineering: single DOM tooltip container + streaming content API (expose showPartial(fields))
Engineering: keyboard focus manager + aria-live summary announcer
Engineering: add perf microbenchmark against sample datasets and wire to perf dashboard
QA: create accessibility regression tests using VoiceOver and NVDA scenarios
Docs: write short guide for integrators describing token usage and modifier-key inspection behavior
